description: Hermes's TextEncoder.prototype.encodeInto passes its destination argument through getTypedArrayBuffer() in JSIUtils.cpp, which reads the `buffer`, `byteOffset`, and `byteLength` properties off the object without verifying the object is a real TypedArray or that the claimed length fits the backing ArrayBuffer. A 646-byte JavaScript PoC supplies a plain object wrapping an 8-byte ArrayBuffer but claiming byteLength 1000000, together with a 100000-character string. convertUTF16ToUTF8BufferWithReplacements then writes UTF-8 output far past the 8-byte heap block. ASAN confirms a heap-buffer-overflow WRITE inside the 8-byte region allocated by JSArrayBuffer::createDataBlock, reproducing identically across three fresh container runs (exit 134).
reproduction: 2. Construct a plain JS object with `buffer` set to that ArrayBuffer, `byteOffset: 0`, and a large spoofed `byteLength` (e.g., 1000000).
3. Call new TextEncoder().encodeInto(largeString, fakeView) with a long string (e.g., 'A'.repeat(100000)).
4. encodeInto writes UTF-8 bytes past the 8-byte allocation, corrupting adjacent heap memory.
technical_details: ASAN: "heap-buffer-overflow on address 0x602000005018 ... WRITE of size 1" in convertUTF16ToUTF8BufferWithReplacements (UTF8.cpp:149:19). The root cause is getTypedArrayBuffer() duck-typing the destination: it trusts user-controlled `byteLength`/`byteOffset` properties instead of validating them against the real ArrayBuffer size, so encodeInto is handed a buffer pointer/length pair where length vastly exceeds the actual 8-byte allocation.
title: Heap-buffer-overflow in hermes.cpp:262
